definitions.supplemental: Piers P. gare : R. Brun. ȝared, pp. prepared : Laym. ȝærwen to make ready : O. Sax. garuwian, gerwean, girwian to make ready, prepare : O. H. Ger. garawén, garwén, garawjan. v. Grm. D. M. 984.
definitions.meaning: To make ready, prepare, procure, supply, put on, clothe

quotations.old_english: Ðú gǽst befóran Drihtnes ansýne, his wegas gearwian
quotations.latin: præibis ante faciem Domini, pārāre vias ejus

quotations.old_english: Óþ on écnysse ic gearwie sǽd ðín
quotations.latin: usque in æternum præpārābo sēmen tuum

quotations.english: he prepares life's way for souls

quotations.old_english: Sumum wundorgiefe þurh goldsmiþe gearwad weorþeþ
quotations.english: to one a wondrous skill in goldsmith's art is provided

quotations.old_english: Gearwian us togénes gréne strǽte up to englum
quotations.english: let us prepare before ourselves a green path to the angels above

quotations.old_english: Ðæt selfe wæter ðegnunge gearwode beforan his fótum
quotations.english: the very water did reverence before his feet

source_text: gearwian, gerwian, gerwan, girwan, gierwan, gyrwan, gyrian, girian, gierian; p. ode, ade, ede; pp. od, ad, ed To make ready, prepare, procure, supply, put on, clothe; p&a-short;r&a-long;re, præp&a-short;r&a-long;re, præst&a-long;re, indu&e-short;re, vest&i-long;re :-- Ðú gǽst befóran Drihtnes ansýne, his wegas gearwian præ&i-long;bis ante faciem D&o-short;m&i-short;ni, p&a-short;r&a-long;re vias ejus, Lk. Bos. 1, 76 : Exon. 58 b; Th. 210, 21; Ph. 189 : 119 a : Th. 456, 27; Hy. 4, 73 : Elen. Kmbl. 1997; El. 1000. Wísdóm oððe snytro gearwiende lytlingum s&a-short;pientiam præstans parv&u-short;lis, Ps. Spl. 18, 8. Óþ on écnysse ic gearwie sǽd ðín usque in æternum præp&a-short;r&a-long;bo s&e-long;men tuum, 88, 4. He lífes weg gǽstum gearwaþ he prepares life's way for souls, Exon. 34 a; Th. 108. 11; Gú. 71 : 117 a; Th. 450, 21; Dóm. 91. Ic gearwode leóhtfæt cyninge mínum p&a-short;r&a-long;vi lucernam Christo meo, Ps. Spl. 131, 18. Ðú gearwodest wlite mínum mægn præst&i-short;tisti d&e-short;c&o-short;ri meo virt&u-long;tem, 29, 8. Grinu hí gearwodon fótum mínum laqueum p&a-short;r&a-long;v&e-long;runt p&e-short;d&i-short;bus meis, Ps. Spl. 56, 8. Sumum wundorgiefe þurh goldsmiþe gearwad weorþeþ to one a wondrous skill in goldsmith's art is provided, Exon. 88 a; Th. 331, 25; Vy. 73. Gearwian us togénes gréne strǽte up to englum let us prepare before ourselves a green path to the angels above, Cd. 219; Th. 282, 15; Sat. 287. Hú gé eówic gearwige quid induamini, Mt. Kmbl. Rush. 6, 25 : 27, 29. Ðæt selfe wæter ðegnunge gearwode beforan his fótum the very water did reverence before his feet, St. And. 22, 19. [Piers P. gare : R. Brun. &yogh;ared, pp. prepared : Laym. &yogh;ærwen to make ready : O. Sax. garuwian, gerwean, girwian to make ready, prepare : O. H. Ger. garawén, garwén, garawjan.] v. Grm. D. M. 984. DER. a-gearwian, ge-.
